State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Shubham Electronics vs Smt.Asha Vishwakarma on 9 May, 2024
Daily Order 

M. P. STATE  CONSUMER  DISPUTES  REDRESSAL  COMMISSION,                         

 PLOT NO.76, ARERA HILLS, BHOPAL

 

 

 

 FIRST APPEAL NO. 323 OF 2018

 

(Arising out of order dated 25.07.2018 passed in C.C.No.101/2017 by District Commission, Chhindwara)

 

 

 

SHUBHAM ELECTRONICS,

 

NEAR INNER GROUND, NAGPUR ROAD,

 

CHHINDWARA (M.P.)                                                                                                  ... APPELLANT.

 

 

 

                  Versus

 

 

 

1. SMT. ASHA VISHWAKARMA,

 

    W/O SHRI GHUDANLAL VISHWAKARMA,

 

    R/O PRAGYAPURAM COLONY, GURAIYA ROAD,

 

    CHHINDWARA (M.P.)

 

 

 

2. BAJAJ FINANCE PVT.LTD. THROUGH MANAGER,

 

    PARASIA ROAD, CHHINDWARA (M.P.)                                                               .... RESPONDENTS.  

 

 

 

 BEFORE :

 

            HON'BLE SHRI A. K. TIWARI                :    ACTING PRESIDENT

 

            HON'BLE DR. SRIKANT PANDEY        :     MEMBER

 

                       

 

 COUNSEL FOR PARTIES :

 

                Shri Ravindra Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellant.

 

            Shri D. K. Sahu, learned counsel for the respondent no.1.

 

            None for the respondent no.2 though served.

 

 

 

 O R D E R
(Passed On 09.05.2024)

 

         The following order of the Commission was delivered by A. K. Tiwari, Acting President:
Being aggrieved by the order dated 25.07.2018 passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Chhindwara (for short 'District Commission) in C.C.No.101/2017 whereby the complaint filed by complainant/respondent no.1 has been allowed, the opposite party no.1/appellant-Shubham Electronics has filed this appeal.
2.                The facts of the case as narrated by the complainant/respondent no.1 (hereinafter referred to as 'complainant') are that She had purchased a 43
-2-
inch Samsung LED TV for a sum of Rs.46,000/- from the opposite party no.1. She after depositing Rs.25,000/- had obtained finance for a sum of Rs.21,000/- from the opposite party no.2-finance company.  The opposite party no.1's engineer installed the TV at her residence and when it was started it is found some lines are displaying on the screen. On complaint being made to the opposite party no.1-it is told that it was due to disc problem. The disc person told that it is company's fault. Again on complaint being made, the opposite party no.1 assured to replace the same within one month. But when the TV was neither repaired nor replaced, the complainant alleging deficiency in service on behalf of opposite parties in supply sub-standard quality of TV approached the District Commission seeking refund of cost of TV or in alternate to replace the TV with new one along with compensation of Rs.10,000/- and costs.
3.                The opposite party no.1 in its reply before the District Commission denying the allegations made in the complaint submitted that after getting all the information, the complainant had purchased the subject TV. Authorised representative technician of the opposite party no.1 after installation started and had given all information regarding operation. After two days the complainant complained about display of lines on the screen. Salesman Krishna Chourasia approached the complainant's house and found that there was physical damage in the LED TV set. Service Engineer Arshad also after inspection found that the two panels of LED were damaged and photo system is also damaged which clearly goes to show that the complainant mishandled the same. In such
-3-
circumstances, the service engineer of the company and the employee of the opposite party no.1 informed her that in case of physical damage and water injury the company is not giving any guarantee/warranty to electronic appliances. The TV damaged due to negligent maintenance of the complainant for which the opposite party no.1 cannot be held liable. There has been no deficiency in service. It is therefore prayed that the complaint be dismissed.
4.                The District Commission allowing the complaint directed the opposite party no.1 to repair the subject LED TV of the complainant within a period of one month or in alternate refund the cost of LED TV Rs.46,000/- to complainant failing which the amount shall carry interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of order till payment. In addition, compensation of Rs.2,000/- with costs of Rs.1,000/- is also awarded.
5.                Heard learned counsel for the parties. Perused the record.
6.                Learned counsel for the appellant/opposite party no.1 argued that the complainant did not implead the service centre as a party to the case. The engineer of the service centre approached the complainant and therefore, it cannot be said that the complaint was not lodged with the service centre. He argued that the District Commission has wrongly concluded that it is responsibility of the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects pointed out in TV and the opposite party no.1 did not attempt to remove the same. In fact, the complainant wants to replace the penal which is not possible. The impugned order passed by the District Commission is against the law. He therefore prayed for setting aside the impugned order.
-4-
7.                Learned counsel for the complainant/respondent no.1 argued that the subject TV was suffering from defect from the day one of its installation. The employee and engineer of the opposite party no.1 inspected the said TV and found defects in the TV i.e. within warranty and therefore, the opposite party no.1 is liable to remove the defects or in alternative to refund the cost of the TV. He argued that the District Commission after appreciating the evidence available on record has rightly passed the impugned order. He therefore prayed for dismissal of appeal.
8.                Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having gone through the record as also the impugned order, we find that immediately after installation of TV defects were found in the TV and this fact was confirmed by Krishna Chourasia, sales man and Engineer Arshad of the opposite party no.1 who found physical damage and click system damage. It is also not denied by the opposite party no.1 that there was no warranty/guarantee of two years on the said product. Thus when the subject TV was within warranty/guarantee period, it is the duty of the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects to the satisfaction of the complainant and when they failed to do so, they have committed deficiency in service.
9.                It is also pertinent to mention here that the opposite party no.1 failed to demonstrate by way of any documentary evidence that the TV got damaged by the complainant as also the physical damage and water injury does not cover under the warranty/guarantee period in case of electronic appliances.
-5-
10.               In view of the foregoing discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the District Commission has committed no error in allowing the complaint and directing the opposite party no.1 to remove the defects or in alternative refund the cost of the TV.  Accordingly, the impugned order passed by the District Commission is hereby affirmed.
11.               In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.  No order as to costs.
(A. K. Tiwari)              (Dr. Srikant Pandey)  

 

                  Acting President                      Member
